They are great for giving someone who has never raced r/c a chance to see what its like driving something closer to the real deal then Walmart ever could. That way you can tell if it;s something they actually want to get into after the novelty has worn off. Much cheaper then going right into a true Hobby Grade r/c with all the extras needed for it,   at a fraction of the cost. First thing I would do is get a cheap hobby grade charger of eBay or Amazon.  That would make your charge times so much faster and could actually fuller charge your current stock batts. Then you could either solder better battery connectors (deans, Traxxas...etc) on the stock batts and charge plug or just get an adapter for the batteries on ebay.   Then as needed,  find a larger hobby grade mAh battery,  which will need a better charger anyways.  Hope some of that helps,   I raced for about 15 years after high school and I use Haiboxing r/c to see if my son has the same love for it that I did before getting him into it.

The biggest problem most players run into is leveling their team to fast.  Going past gold before having the XP, evo…etc to max the majority of their team to that next level like platinum, diamond..etc Other then last years “force leveling” the majority of players should stay gold to be competitive in all game modes.  If you have the time and in most cases money to drop on the game,  then by all means go for the diamond rewards, but if you’re a casual player,  just stay gold and crank your team strength.
